senses.definition: Something you do often, usually without having to think about it.
senses.example: Putting my shoes by the door is a habit that helps me get ready.

senses.definition: The breaking of one large natural home into smaller pieces separated by roads, buildings, or other barriers.
senses.example: The new roads caused habitat fragmentation where one forest once stood.

senses.definition: To cut with rough, strong blows.
senses.example: The gardener hacked at a thick vine that blocked the path.

senses.definition: A clever shortcut or trick that makes a task easier.
senses.example: I learned a drawing hack for making two circles the same size.

senses.definition: A kind of fish found in the northern Atlantic Ocean that people sometimes eat.
senses.example: My grandfather ordered baked haddock for dinner.

senses.definition: A short kind of poem that began in Japan and often notices a brief moment in nature.
senses.example: Her haiku described a cold drop of rain on a fence.

senses.definition: Small balls or pieces of ice that fall from a storm cloud.
senses.example: Hail rattled on the metal roof.

senses.definition: To call out to someone or signal for someone to stop.
senses.example: We stood by the curb to hail a taxi.

senses.definition: A tool with rows of stiff hairs or pins for making hair smooth and neat.
senses.example: I used my hairbrush after the wind tangled my hair.

senses.definition: A cut or trim of someone’s hair, or the style it has after that.
senses.example: After my haircut, my bangs no longer covered my eyes.

senses.definition: A bent piece of wire or plastic used to hold hair in place.
senses.example: A hairpin kept the loose braid from falling in my eyes.

senses.definition: Bending very sharply back in nearly the opposite direction.
senses.example: The bus slowed before the hairpin turn.

senses.definition: One of two equal parts of something.
senses.example: We each ate half of the sandwich.

senses.definition: About halfway or only partly.
senses.example: I was half awake when the phone rang.

senses.definition: At or near the middle of a distance or task.
senses.example: We stopped halfway up the hill to drink some water.

senses.definition: A passage inside a building that leads to other rooms.
senses.example: I followed the hallway until I found the art room.

senses.definition: To stop or cause something to stop.
senses.example: The red flag told the runners to halt.

senses.definition: A stop in movement or activity.
senses.example: The wagon came to a halt at the gate.

senses.definition: A piece of cloth or netting hung at both ends so a person can rest in it.
senses.example: The hammock swung gently between the trees.

senses.definition: A large container for things such as dirty clothes or picnic food.
senses.example: I dropped my shirt in the laundry hamper.

senses.definition: To make it harder for someone to do something or move freely.
senses.example: A fallen branch hampered our efforts to clear the trail.

senses.definition: The part at the end of your arm that has fingers and a thumb.
senses.example: I waved my hand so the coach could see me.

senses.definition: One of the moving pointers on a clock.
senses.example: The long hand pointed at the six.

senses.definition: To give something to someone, often by holding it out to them.
senses.example: Please hand me the blue marker.

senses.definition: To give someone work or a form that they asked you to turn in.
senses.example: Please hand in your drawing before we leave the art room.

senses.definition: As much as you can hold in one hand.
senses.example: I scattered a handful of seeds over the bare patch.

senses.definition: A small number of people or things.
senses.example: Only a handful of people stayed until the end of the game.

senses.definition: The part of an object you hold to use, move, or open it.
senses.example: Turn the handle to open the door.

senses.definition: To deal with a task or problem.
senses.example: We can handle the mess if we each clean one part.

senses.definition: A bar that you can hold on to as you go along a path or stairs.
senses.example: I held the handrail while carrying a stack of books downstairs.

senses.definition: A greeting or sign of agreement in which two people hold and briefly shake hands.
senses.example: The players ended the match with a handshake.

senses.definition: Good-looking, often in a strong or neat way.
senses.example: The painting showed a handsome horse with a shiny coat.

senses.definition: A position in which you balance upside down on your hands.
senses.example: He held a handstand for three seconds.

senses.definition: Writing made by hand, or the particular way someone forms their letters.
senses.example: I recognized my grandmother’s handwriting on the envelope.

senses.definition: Useful or easy to use.
senses.example: The little hook was handy for holding our keys.

senses.definition: Close by and ready to use.
senses.example: Keep a pencil handy while you read.

senses.definition: Good at making or fixing things with your hands.
senses.example: Our handy neighbor repaired the broken hinge.

senses.definition: To hold or be held from above so the rest dangles down.
senses.example: We hung three paintings in the hall.

senses.definition: To keep trying or wait patiently when something is hard or slow.
senses.example: Hang in there. The last piece of the puzzle might be under the box.

senses.definition: A large building where aircraft are kept or repaired.
senses.example: The plane rolled slowly into the hangar.

senses.definition: A shape with a hook that holds up a piece of clothing.
senses.example: I put the clean shirt on a hanger.

senses.definition: A nest attached above itself to something like twigs so its bottom hangs free.
senses.example: A Baltimore oriole weaves a hanging nest that looks like a small bag.

senses.definition: To take place.
senses.example: The puppet show will happen right after lunch.

senses.definition: The feeling of being glad or pleased about something.
senses.example: I felt a burst of happiness when my missing dog came home.

senses.definition: Feeling pleased or glad.
senses.example: I was happy when my cousin came to visit.

senses.definition: An area of deep enough water where boats can stay with some shelter from wind and waves.
senses.example: The ferry waited in the harbor while the weather improved.

senses.definition: To give someone or something a place to stay or hide.
senses.example: The old barn harbored several owls.

senses.definition: Firm and difficult to bend, cut, or press into.
senses.example: The water in the tray froze into hard ice.

senses.definition: Difficult to do or understand.
senses.example: The last question was hard, so we worked on it together.

senses.definition: With a lot of force or effort.
senses.example: Lee worked hard to finish the puzzle.

senses.definition: To make or become harder or more solid.
senses.example: The clay hardened while it sat in the sun.

senses.definition: Almost not at all or only by a small amount.
senses.example: I could hardly hear the music from my room.

senses.definition: The physical parts of a computer or other device that you could touch.
senses.example: The screen is part of the tablet’s hardware.

senses.definition: An animal related to a rabbit, often with longer ears and longer legs.
senses.example: A hare ran swiftly across the snowy field.

senses.definition: Damage or hurt done to someone or something.
senses.example: The storm did little harm to the plants under cover.

senses.definition: To hurt or damage.
senses.example: Too much salt can harm the grass beside the road.

senses.definition: Able to cause damage or hurt someone or something.
senses.example: Smoke can be harmful to the lungs.

senses.definition: Not causing harm or damage.
senses.example: The funny-looking shadow was a harmless pile of books.

senses.definition: A small musical instrument that you hold to your lips and play by breathing through holes.
senses.example: She played a short tune on her harmonica.

senses.definition: Two or more notes sounding together, or the way groups of notes fit with a tune.
senses.example: The second singer added harmony below the tune.

senses.definition: A set of straps used to hold or control a person, animal, or object.
senses.example: The dog wore a harness with a clip for its leash.

senses.definition: To attach a set of straps, or to put a source of power to use.
senses.example: Our little water wheel harnessed the force of the flowing creek.

senses.definition: A musical instrument with many strings held in a frame and played by plucking.
senses.example: The harp made a soft ringing sound as the player touched each string.

senses.definition: Rough, unpleasant, or severe.
senses.example: The harsh light made me squint.

senses.definition: Unkind or stricter than needed.
senses.example: A harsh remark can make someone feel small.

senses.definition: The food or other crops gathered when they are ready, or the time of gathering them.
senses.example: The late frost made the apple harvest smaller this year.

senses.definition: To gather a crop when it is ready.
senses.example: We harvest the beans after the pods grow long and firm.

senses.definition: A hurry to get something done, sometimes so fast that mistakes happen.
senses.example: In her haste to leave, Ana put on two different shoes.

senses.definition: A cover for your head, sometimes with an edge that sticks out to shade your eyes.
senses.example: I wore a wide hat on our sunny walk.

senses.definition: To break out of an egg or help an egg reach that stage.
senses.example: The chicks hatched a day apart.

senses.definition: A small opening with a cover, often in a roof, floor, ship, or vehicle.
senses.example: We opened the attic hatch to get the folding ladder.

senses.definition: A young animal that recently came out of an egg.
senses.example: We saw the tiny turtle hatchling move toward the water.

senses.definition: To feel very strong dislike for someone or something.
senses.example: I hate the sound of a chair scraping across the floor.

senses.definition: A feeling of very strong dislike.
senses.example: The story showed how hate can grow when people refuse to listen to each other.

senses.definition: Acting as if you are much better or more important than other people.
senses.example: The haughty king refused to listen to the gardener's idea.

senses.definition: To pull or carry something that is heavy or hard to move.
senses.example: Two friends helped haul the wagon up the hill.

senses.definition: In stories, to visit a place again and again as a ghost.
senses.example: In the story, a friendly ghost haunted the empty theater.

senses.definition: To stay in someone’s mind and keep bothering them.
senses.example: The unfinished drawing haunted me until I worked out how to end it.

senses.definition: To give a reason or idea that makes sense and is worth thinking about.
senses.example: You have a point about the loose strap. Let’s check it before we go.

senses.definition: A calm or safe place where someone or something can rest or find shelter.
senses.example: The sheltered pool was a haven for ducks when the wind blew.

senses.definition: A lot of damage, confusion, or disorder.
senses.example: A puppy ran through our neat paper town and caused havoc.

senses.definition: A bird with sharp claws and a hooked beak that hunts other animals for food.
senses.example: A hawk circled over the field, watching for movement.

senses.definition: A large pile of dried grass saved as food for animals.
senses.example: The small barn stood next to a tall haystack.

senses.definition: Out of control or not working as planned, especially in the phrase “go haywire.”
senses.example: Our homemade robot went haywire and turned in circles.

senses.definition: Greenish brown or a mixture of light brown and green, often describing eyes.
senses.example: My cousin has hazel eyes that look greener in sunlight.

senses.definition: A shrub or small tree that produces hazelnuts.
senses.example: A hazel grew beside the low stone wall.

senses.definition: Hard to see through because of fine particles or water drops in the air.
senses.example: The mountain looked hazy from across the valley.

senses.definition: Not clear or well remembered.
senses.example: My memory of our first camping trip is hazy.

senses.definition: The part of your body that contains your brain and face.
senses.example: Eli pulled a warm hat over his head.

senses.definition: The person in charge of a group.
senses.example: The head of our club handed out the jobs.

senses.definition: To move toward a place.
senses.example: Let’s head home before dark.

senses.definition: A pain in your head.
senses.example: The bright lights made my headache feel worse.

senses.definition: A problem that is annoying or troublesome.
senses.example: Finding seats for everyone was a headache.

senses.definition: A narrow band worn around the head to hold back hair or catch sweat.
senses.example: She wore a green headband during the race.

senses.definition: A title that tells what a section of writing is about.
senses.example: The heading told us that this part was about frogs.

senses.definition: The direction a vehicle is pointing.
senses.example: The pilot checked the plane's heading before turning.

senses.definition: A form of “head” used to say that someone or something is going in a particular direction.
senses.example: We were heading home when the rain started.

senses.definition: A light worn on the head or fixed to the front of a vehicle.
senses.example: My headlamp lit the inside of my tent.

senses.definition: A light on the front of a vehicle that shines ahead.
senses.example: She turned on a headlight when the sky grew dark.

senses.definition: The title across the top of a news story.
senses.example: The headline told us the library would reopen on Friday.

senses.definition: To be the main person or event listed in a performance or story.
senses.example: Our school choir will headline the evening concert.

senses.definition: A padded part of a seat that can support the back of a person's head.
senses.example: I lowered the headrest on the chair.

senses.definition: Progress toward finishing or solving something.
senses.example: We made headway on the puzzle once we found the corner pieces.

senses.definition: Wind blowing toward the front of someone or something moving ahead.
senses.example: The cyclist had to push harder into the headwind.

senses.definition: To become healthy again or help someone or something get better after harm.
senses.example: It took a few days for the scrape on my knee to heal.

senses.definition: Well and working as it should.
senses.example: The healthy plant had several new leaves.

senses.definition: Helping you or another living thing stay well.
senses.example: We packed a healthy lunch before the hike.

senses.definition: A pile that has no special order or shape.
senses.example: A heap of leaves blew against the fence.

senses.definition: To pile up in a large amount.
senses.example: We heaped the branches in the wheelbarrow.

senses.definition: To notice sounds with your ears.
senses.example: Can you hear the rain on the roof?

senses.definition: To learn about something from a person or message.
senses.example: We heard that the next game would be on Saturday.

senses.definition: The organ that pumps blood around the body.
senses.example: My heart beat faster when I ran uphill.

senses.definition: The center or most important part of something.
senses.example: Working together is at the heart of our club.

senses.definition: A shape with two rounded parts at the top and a point below.
senses.example: We cut a heart out of folded red paper.

senses.definition: Deep sadness, especially about someone or something you care about.
senses.example: She felt heartache when her closest friend moved away.

senses.definition: The floor of a fireplace or the area directly in front of it.
senses.example: We sat on a rug beside the stone hearth.

senses.definition: Filling and enough to satisfy hunger.
senses.example: A bowl of hearty stew warmed us after the hike.

senses.definition: Warm, strong, and full of energy.
senses.example: Our coach greeted us with a hearty laugh.

senses.definition: Energy that moves from a warmer object or place to a cooler one because of that difference in temperature.
senses.example: Heat moved from the hot soup into the metal spoon.

senses.definition: A machine that uses energy to move heat from one place to another.
senses.example: A heat pump can move warmth from the outdoors into a house.

senses.definition: To lift, pull, or throw something with great effort.
senses.example: It took both of us to heave the trunk onto the porch.

senses.definition: To rise and fall with a strong movement.
senses.example: The waves made the deck heave up and down.

senses.definition: Weighing a lot or hard to lift.
senses.example: The heavy box needed two people to carry it.

senses.definition: Very strong or large in amount.
senses.example: Heavy rain filled the puddles in minutes.

senses.definition: A row of bushes grown as a wall between places.
senses.example: Sparrows hid in the hedge beside the road.

senses.definition: To answer carefully without taking a clear side.
senses.example: He hedged when asked which poster was best, since he liked both.

senses.definition: A small animal with stiff spines on its back that can roll into a ball.
senses.example: The picture showed a hedgehog curled up under some leaves.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a warning or advice and take it seriously.
senses.example: The hikers heeded the sign and stayed on the marked path.

senses.definition: The back part of a foot, or the part of a shoe beneath it.
senses.example: A pebble had slipped under my heel.

senses.definition: Heavy, large, or greater than usual.
senses.example: The recipe book was so hefty that I carried it with both hands.

senses.definition: The distance from the bottom of something to its top, or how tall a person or object is.
senses.example: We measured the height of the plant from the soil to its top leaf.

senses.definition: To raise or make stronger.
senses.example: The quiet music heightened the suspense in the play.

senses.definition: A person who is set to receive property or a title from someone else, often when that person dies.
senses.example: In the story, the prince was the heir to the throne.

senses.definition: A hard or padded cover worn on your head for protection.
senses.example: I buckled my helmet before riding my bike.

senses.definition: To make it easier for someone to do something.
senses.example: Could you help me carry this stack of books?

senses.definition: Things someone does or gives to make a task easier.
senses.example: With Aunt Rae’s help, we put the shelf together.

senses.definition: Making a task easier or giving someone useful support.
senses.example: The signs were helpful when we looked for the exit.

senses.definition: One half of a ball-shaped object, especially one half of Earth.
senses.example: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.

senses.definition: A material in red blood cells that can pick up oxygen and let it go again.
senses.example: Hemoglobin gives red blood cells their color.

senses.definition: To be a sign that something is coming or to announce it.
senses.example: The first green shoots heralded the return of spring.

senses.definition: A person sent to make an important announcement.
senses.example: In the play, a herald arrived to tell the town about the contest.

senses.definition: An animal that eats mainly or only plants.
senses.example: Triceratops had a beak and teeth to feed as a herbivore.

senses.definition: A large group of animals that live, feed, or travel together.
senses.example: We stopped to watch a herd of deer cross the open field.

senses.definition: To guide a group of animals or people in a certain direction.
senses.example: The dog helped herd the sheep into the pen.

senses.definition: In or to the place where you are or where you are pointing.
senses.example: Put the puzzle pieces here on this shelf.

senses.definition: Someone admired for bravery, kindness, or an important action.
senses.example: To our family, the neighbor who found our lost dog was a hero.

senses.definition: The main character you hope will succeed in a story.
senses.example: The hero follows a trail through an underground city.

senses.definition: Great courage shown while facing trouble or helping others.
senses.example: The memorial tells the story of the rescuers' heroism.

senses.definition: To pause before you act or speak because you are unsure.
senses.example: Nia hesitated at the fork, then chose the path with the blue signs.

senses.definition: A short pause before doing something because you are not sure.
senses.example: After a moment of hesitation, I raised my hand.

senses.definition: A long period when an animal’s body slows down to use less energy, often during winter.
senses.example: The groundhog went into hibernation beneath the ground.

senses.definition: A sudden sound you make when a breathing muscle tightens by itself and the parts of your throat that make your voice close briefly.
senses.example: My first hiccup made me stop in the middle of a sentence.

senses.definition: A small problem that slows something down for a little while.
senses.example: A missing cable was the only hiccup before the show.

senses.definition: A kind of tree that produces nuts and has hard wood.
senses.example: We found a hickory with its nuts scattered under the tree.

senses.definition: Kept out of sight or hard to find.
senses.example: The hidden door looked like part of the wall.

senses.definition: A form of “hide” used after “has,” “have,” or “had.”
senses.example: I had hidden the gift in a basket.

senses.definition: To put yourself or something else where it cannot easily be seen or found.
senses.example: She hid behind the tree during the game.

senses.definition: The skin of a large animal, sometimes prepared for use as leather.
senses.example: The old drum had a cover made from an animal hide.

senses.definition: A private or hidden place where someone can go.
senses.example: We made a hideaway out of blankets behind the couch.

senses.definition: One sign in a writing system that uses picture-like shapes to stand for sounds, words, or ideas. Ancient Egyptians used such signs.
senses.example: This hieroglyph looks like a bird, but it can be used to write a sound.

senses.definition: An area of land that stands high above the country around it.
senses.example: The days in the highlands were cooler than at the coast.

senses.definition: A long walk, often along a trail or in the countryside.
senses.example: We took a hike around the lake.

senses.definition: To go on a long walk.
senses.example: Our class hiked to the top of the hill.

senses.definition: A person who takes a long walk, often on a trail in nature.
senses.example: Each hiker carried water and a snack.

senses.definition: An area of land that rises higher than the land around it and is usually lower than a mountain.
senses.example: We carried our sleds to the top of the hill.

senses.definition: The sloping side of a hill.
senses.example: Wildflowers grew on the sunny hillside.

senses.definition: The highest part of a hill.
senses.example: From the hilltop, I could see the winding path below us.

senses.definition: At the back of an animal's body.
senses.example: The rabbit stood on its hind legs.

senses.definition: To slow down progress or make an action more difficult.
senses.example: The strong wind hindered our walk across the field.

senses.definition: A joint made of two parts that lets a door, lid, or other piece swing open and shut.
senses.example: One hinge squeaked each time the door opened.

senses.definition: A rod that goes through parts of a hinge so they can turn around it together.
senses.example: The door swung around its hinge pins each time we opened it.

senses.definition: A small clue that helps you figure something out.
senses.example: The teacher gave us a hint about where to look.

senses.definition: To suggest something without saying it directly.
senses.example: Rae hinted at the surprise by asking what kind of cake I liked.

senses.definition: The part on either side of your body between your waist and the top of your leg.
senses.example: I balanced the bag against my hip.

senses.definition: A short name for a hippopotamus, a very large African animal that spends much of its day in water.
senses.example: The hippo's eyes and ears stuck up above the water.

senses.definition: To pay someone to do a job.
senses.example: The shop hired Jay to deliver groceries.
